data.summary: Replace ad-hoc session token reads scattered across routes with a centralized auth middleware, fixing the compliance issue where tokens leak into request logs.

options.name: Edge middleware
options.summary: Validate the session in a single middleware that runs before any route handler.
cons: All routes need same auth shape
options.whenToUse: When auth requirements are uniform across the API surface.

options.name: Per-route guards
options.summary: Each route imports and calls a guard helper at the top.
cons: Must remember on every new route
options.whenToUse: When per-route auth requirements vary significantly.

options.name: Decorator pattern
options.summary: Wrap each handler with a withAuth() higher-order function.
cons: Harder for new contributors to grok
options.whenToUse: When auth has multiple variants composed of smaller checks.

data.beforeMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A[read cookie] --> B[parse token]
  B --> C[log full headers]
  C --> D[fetch user]
data.afterMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A[read cookie] --> B[validate via lib/auth]
  B --> C[fetch user]

data.beforeMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A[parse body] --> B[verify password]
  B --> C[issue token]
  C --> D[Set-Cookie token]
  D --> E[return 200]
data.afterMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A[parse body] --> B[verify password]
  B --> C[create session row]
  C --> D[Set-Cookie sid HttpOnly Secure]
  D --> E[set CSRF token]
  E --> F[return 200]

data.rule: Session token written to access log
data.rationale: The previous middleware logged the full request including the Authorization header. Tokens ended up in access logs that compliance flagged in the last quarterly review.
Set-Cookie does not declare SameSite. Browsers default to Lax but explicit Strict prevents CSRF in cross-site iframe scenarios.

tour.title: Why this refactor
tour.caption: Compliance flagged session tokens leaking into access logs. This PR centralizes auth so there's one place to audit and one place to redact.

tour.title: What it touches
tour.caption: Five modules see edits — middleware, auth, session, db/sessions, logger. The api/* routes themselves stay untouched.

tour.title: The decision
tour.caption: Edge middleware won over per-route guards and a decorator pattern. Compliance wanted a single file to audit; the trade-off is that all routes need the same auth shape.

tour.title: The simplification
tour.caption: getSession() loses the explicit header logging and delegates token validation to lib/auth — four steps down to three.

tour.title: The hardening
tour.caption: Login now creates a session row, sets HttpOnly + Secure cookie attributes, and issues a CSRF token. One step longer but materially safer.

tour.title: The root-cause risk
tour.caption: The reason this PR exists — full request headers were being logged, leaking Authorization tokens to access logs.

tour.title: The leftover
tour.caption: Cookie Set-Cookie still doesn't declare SameSite. Lax is the browser default, but explicit Strict closes CSRF in iframe scenarios.

tour.title: Total footprint
tour.caption: Seven files, +156 / −98. The bulk is the new lib/auth.ts that the middleware delegates to.
